overall_summary: Three separate bear cubs play on a backyard trampoline while one older woman enters through the visible upper-right gate, crosses the open grass, reaches the lower-left trampoline steps, climbs them, and joins the cubs.
tone: Unplanned real-life nighttime home-security footage: ordinary, observational, imperfect, funny because the event is unexpectedly real, never cinematic or commercial.
capture_style: One fixed elevated outdoor security-camera viewpoint with mild fisheye distortion, grain, limited dynamic range, and no camera movement.
visual_style: A fenced suburban backyard at night with one trampoline, one short set of steps at its lower-left edge, one gate at the upper-right fence line, and a clear grass route between them.
visual_realism: The gate, grass route, trampoline, steps, Grandma, and three cubs must remain in one continuous physical layout with realistic scale and contact.
audio_policy: Natural location sound only: faint night ambience, footsteps, gate movement, trampoline springs, mat movement, and bear cub sounds.
camera_lock: Keep the same wide elevated security-camera viewpoint, horizon, lens character, fence, gate, route, trampoline, and steps throughout. No cuts, pans, tilts, zooms, or alternate views.
continuity_invariants: Exactly one older woman and exactly three separate bear cubs; no duplicates or morphing.
Grandma's only route is upper-right gate, open grass, lower-left steps, then trampoline.
Grandma must be visibly on the ground at the gate, during the crossing, and at the bottom of the steps before climbing.
Grandma's scale must remain natural relative to the trampoline, steps, fence, and cubs.
The three cubs remain on the trampoline and retain stable scale and identity.
